meeting_header: Recorded: 2027-06-12 08:00 PT | Duration: 52 mins | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Reed (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Hudson), Tom Delaney (Hudson Security), Liam O'Neill (Hudson SRE)
summary: Discovery focused on connecting Hudson's multi-account AWS environment to Redwood Private. Key constraints: cross-account access, egress IPs, KMS + audit logging, region gating for EU data, and preference to avoid NAT hairpinning. Agreed to share diagrams and run initial latency tests before pilot.
topics: Cross-account PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway options
KMS / key access and encryption boundary
Region constraints and data residency (EU nodes)
Audit logging, SOC2 evidence, and SSO integration
transcript:
00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya Patel from Redwood, I'll run the call, with Jonas our SE. Quick roll call?
00:07 Priya (Hudson): Priya here, Platform eng. Hey.
00:10 Tom (Hudson Security): Tom Delaney, security. Liam's joining in a sec.
00:14 Liam (Hudson SRE): Sorry running late, Liam O'Neill, SRE.
00:18 Maya: Great. Quick agenda: understand your network topology, cross-account constraints, regional gating, and then options for private connectivity — PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, or dedicated peering.
00:32 Jonas (Redwood SE): I'll add, we'll also outline what we need for IP allocations, KMS access, and egress IPs so you can plan firewall rules.
00:40 Priya: Perfect. Current setup: we have three AWS org accounts — dev/test/prod — each with their own VPCs. Prod is in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. We're trying to avoid opening public egress from prod.
00:58 Tom: From security side we need to ensure no data leaves EU for EU-customer workloads and also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. SOC2 is a requirement.
01:10 Maya: Totally understood. When you say "avoid opening public egress" do you mean you need no public internet at all, or controlled egress via NGW?
01:18 Priya: For the EU workloads, no public egress. For US it's okay to have curated egress but we'd prefer to hit Redwood over private endpoints.
01:26 Jonas: Ok, two patterns: cross-account AWS PrivateLink where you create interface endpoints in each account pointing to Redwood's service, or a Transit Gateway peering model with an S3-style private endpoint — well not S3 — sorry, TGW + VPC attachments. PrivateLink is per-account but usually simpler for CIDR limitations; TGW centralizes routing but needs wider IP planning.
01:50 Liam: Quick Q — does Redwood support cross-account endpoint service where we accept the VPC endpoint from our account? We try to avoid sharing full route tables.
01:58 Jonas: Yes, we can expose an endpoint service that you create an interface endpoint for — that's cross-account. The acceptance flow can be automated. One catch: interface endpoints need IPs and ENIs in each AZ; if you've got tight IP ranges that matters.
02:12 Priya: Our prod VPC in eu-west-1 is a /27 actually, because of poor planning ages ago, so IP space is tight. TGW might be tricky then.
02:22 Maya: That's good to flag — if the CIDR is a /27 then interface endpoints may exhaust IPs depending on AZs. We usually provide an IP planning template — we'll send that.
02:32 Tom: On KMS, we need to ensure keys never leave our control. Can Redwood accept customer-managed KMS where we grant decrypt/ encrypt to the service role? Or you require Redwood-managed keys?
02:44 Jonas: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) in a couple of modes. For the Private option we can integrate with your KMS — you'd create a key policy allowing the Redwood service principal to use it. We need the key ARN and a cross-account IAM role. I'll detail exact IAM policies.
03:00 Priya: And for audit logs, can we push call-level logs to our S3 bucket? We want to retain them for 12 months and pipe to SIEM.
03:08 Maya: Yes, audit logs are available for Private deployments; we can forward to your S3/CloudWatch. There is also an option to stream to your Kinesis. We'll include that in the docs.
03:18 Liam: Latency — if we do PrivateLink across region boundary, say US->EU fallback, what's typical? Our LLM calls are sensitive to mid-100ms increases.
03:28 Jonas: Latency is primarily network RTT. If the host model is in eu-west-1 and a client in us-east-1 hits it, that's expected higher. For cross-region requests we recommend model pinning to region to avoid transatlantic hops. For EU data residency you'd probably want Redwood nodes in eu-west-1.
03:46 Priya: We do want EU-only for certain datasets. So we need a way to ensure calls from EU prod always route to EU model endpoints.
03:54 Maya: That is policy-level routing — we support region pinning in our routing layer. For Private deployments we'll provision endpoints in the region you choose and set routing policy so EU account hits EU infra only.
04:06 Tom: About NAT/Gateway — we can't have egress from eu-prod to public, so how do we handle updates or container image pulls?
04:15 Jonas: Typically you'd allow a restricted egress path through a proxy or a controlled NAT that only accesses approved hosts. For Redwood managed nodes, if you want air-gapped we'd discuss an on-prem bundle. But for VPC PrivateLink/Private endpoint we don't require outbound internet from your prod instances to call us. The connection is inbound from your VPC to Redwood service via ENI.
04:37 Priya: That helps. One of our constraints: cross-account cost allocation — interface endpoints cost more per AZ, TGW has transit charges. Cost might sway the executive sponsor.
04:48 Maya: We'll include rough TCO comparisons in the doc deck — PrivateLink vs TGW vs Dedicated peering, with cost per month estimates assuming X calls/min. We'll need your expected QPS to model real numbers.
05:00 Liam: Q on IPs again — if we do PrivateLink, ENIs appear in our subnet. That could break our host quotas, right?
05:07 Jonas: Yes, they consume an IP per AZ per endpoint. For multi-AZ HA, it's common to need 3-6 IPs. If CIDR is tiny, you may prefer a centralized proxy account with larger ranges and route via TGW.
05:20 Tom: For compliance, does Redwood have SOC2 Type II and will you share the report under NDA?
05:27 Maya: We do — Redwood is SOC2 Type II and ISO attested. I'll send the redacted report and the security whitepaper.
05:34 Priya: Also SSO — we use Okta. How does auth work for the private control plane — SAML or OIDC?
05:41 Jonas: We integrate with SAML/Okta for the control plane. For the data plane we rely on signed requests and mutual TLS where applicable. We'll include the recommended configuration.
05:52 Liam: Any quirks with cross-account KMS? We saw another vendor require key policies that were impossible in our set-up.
05:59 Jonas: We try to avoid needing full admin access. Typically we ask you to add a key usage policy line granting our service principal Encrypt/Decrypt. If the org requires an activation step, we'll walkthrough it.
06:09 Priya: Great. Can you support IP allowlisting at your side? We need predictable egress IPs to open in our firewall for the return traffic pattern.
06:19 Maya: For PrivateLink the traffic is inside your VPC so outgoing IPs are your ENIs; for outbound callbacks from Redwood (e.g., webhooks) we can provide fixed egress IPs from your region or use a peered NAT in your account. We'll detail both options.
06:34 Tom: One more: cross-account resource acceptance — will Redwood be able to accept interface endpoint connection requests automatically or do we need manual acceptance per account?
06:44 Jonas: We support automated acceptance if you set org-level permissions; otherwise manual accept per endpoint is quick but needs an operator. For scale across many accounts we recommend a CloudFormation stack we provide to standardize endpoint creation.
06:58 Priya: Can you send that CFN template?
07:00 Maya: Absolutely — that's on the action items list.
07:03 Liam: On benchmarking — can you share an example payload and what tokenization and model sizes you expect us to test?
07:10 Jonas: We'll send a bench harness with sample prompts and an example of steady-state token throughput. We'll also indicate how to capture tail-latency percentiles. If you want, Redwood can run an assisted benchmark if you grant staging access.
07:22 Priya: We likely will run in-house first.
07:25 Tom: Any blockers we should be aware of?
07:27 Maya: Main blockers are tight CIDRs and KMS policy approvals. If those are solved we can stand up a pilot within weeks. Also confirm EU region availability for the model you plan to use — some variants may not be deployed in eu-west-1 by default.
07:44 Priya: Which models are in EU today?
07:47 Jonas: We maintain a region catalog; I'll attach it. Short list: open-guan-... sorry, the names sometimes get fuzzy in transcription — but we'll attach model availability per region in the doc.
07:59 Maya: Let's recap action items and next steps.
08:02 Maya: Maya: Redwood to send PrivateLink vs TGW deck, CFN template, IP planning sheet, SOC2/ISO docs. Jonas: bench template and latency test instructions. Priya: share accounts and CIDRs. Follow up meeting 2027-06-19 10:00 AM PT.
08:20 Tom: Sounds good. Thanks all.
08:22 Liam: Thanks.
08:24 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and docs. End.
